## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(I_{r,n-r}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq(n-r)^r\}\), \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has Schur basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and multiplication is LR multiplication truncated to that box. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218; 263-269]
- [proved] For \(A=\Lambda/I_{6,5}\), \(A_+=(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5)\).
- [proved] In each degree \(d\), the complete Pieri rows \(h_t\bar s_\lambda\), \(1\le t\le5\), with \(22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6\) and \(|\lambda|=d-t\), present \((A_+J)_d\) and are exactly the rows used by the artifact’s `lower=[2,2,0,0,0,0]`, `upper=[5,5,5,5,5,5]`, `hDegrees=[1,2,3,4,5]` construction.

## Strategy
Write \(h_t=s_{(t)}\). Jacobi–Trudi expresses every \(s_\lambda\) as a polynomial in the \(h_t\); hence
\[
\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots].
\]
For \(t>5\), \((t)\nsubseteq5^6\), so \(\bar h_t=\bar s_{(t)}=0\) in \(A\). Therefore every positive-degree homogeneous element of \(A\) is a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear combination of positive-degree monomials in \(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5\), each divisible by one \(\bar h_t\). Thus
\[
A_+\subseteq(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5).
\]
The reverse inclusion holds since each \(\bar h_t\) has positive degree. Hence
\[
A_+=(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5). \tag{1}
\]

Let
\[
J_d=\bigoplus_{\substack{22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6\\|\lambda|=d}}
\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda .
\]
The LR containment condition says every nonzero \(\bar s_\alpha\bar s_\lambda\) is a sum of \(\bar s_\nu\) with \(\lambda\subseteq\nu\subseteq5^6\). Thus \(22\subseteq\lambda\) implies \(22\subseteq\nu\), so \(AJ=J\). From (1),
\[
A_+J=\sum_{t=1}^5\bar h_tJ. \tag{2}
\]
Taking degree \(d\),
\[
(A_+J)_d=\sum_{t=1}^5\ \sum_{\substack{22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6\\|\lambda|=d-t}}
\mathbb Z\,\bar h_t\bar s_\lambda. \tag{3}
\]

Order the degree-\(d\) column basis by the artifact convention:
\[
C_d=\{\mu:22\subseteq\mu\subseteq5^6,\ |\mu|=d\},
\]
in reverse lexicographic partition order. Order rows first by \(t=1,\ldots,5\), then by the same order on
\[
\lambda\in C_{d-t}.
\]
Pieri gives, in this column basis,
\[
\bar h_t\bar s_\lambda
 =\sum_{\substack{\mu\in C_d\\\mu/\lambda\text{ a horizontal }t\text{-strip}}}
 \bar s_\mu. \tag{4}
\]
Thus the row indexed by \((t,\lambda)\) has entry
\[
M_d[(t,\lambda),\mu]=
\begin{cases}
1,&\mu/\lambda\text{ is a horizontal }t\text{-strip},\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
This is precisely the complete bounded partition-Pieri row specified by the artifact. Equation (3) proves that its row lattice is exactly \((A_+J)_d\).

Boundary cases are explicit: \(J_d=0\) for \(d<4\) and \(d>30\); for \(d=4\), \(C_4=\{22\}\) and there are no source rows. In degrees \(4\le d\le30\), the rows are exactly those in (4), including any zero rows caused by box truncation. Outside this range the target module is zero.

No determinant, unit, or Smith witness is used in this certificate.

## Gaps
None for this certificate. It establishes only the positive-degree-generator and complete-row presentation facts, not any parent minimality claim.
